Enum Class OperationType

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Enum<OperationType>
com.macstab.chaos.jvm.api.OperationType
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, Comparable<OperationType>, Constable
public enum OperationType extends Enum<OperationType>
Identifies the JVM operation being intercepted or the lifecycle event being signalled.

Each value maps to a specific instrumentation point installed by the agent. Selectors declare which operation types they match; the runtime evaluates active scenarios only when the corresponding instrumentation fires.

Valid selector ↔ operation pairings:

  • ChaosSelector.ThreadSelector — THREAD_START, VIRTUAL_THREAD_START
  • ChaosSelector.ExecutorSelector — EXECUTOR_SUBMIT, EXECUTOR_WORKER_RUN, EXECUTOR_SHUTDOWN, EXECUTOR_AWAIT_TERMINATION
  • ChaosSelector.QueueSelector — QUEUE_PUT, QUEUE_OFFER, QUEUE_TAKE, QUEUE_POLL
  • ChaosSelector.AsyncSelector — ASYNC_COMPLETE, ASYNC_COMPLETE_EXCEPTIONALLY, ASYNC_CANCEL
  • ChaosSelector.SchedulingSelector — SCHEDULE_SUBMIT, SCHEDULE_TICK
  • ChaosSelector.ShutdownSelector — SHUTDOWN_HOOK_REGISTER, EXECUTOR_SHUTDOWN, EXECUTOR_AWAIT_TERMINATION
  • ChaosSelector.ClassLoadingSelector — CLASS_LOAD, CLASS_DEFINE, RESOURCE_LOAD
  • ChaosSelector.MethodSelector — METHOD_ENTER, METHOD_EXIT
  • ChaosSelector.MonitorSelector — MONITOR_ENTER, THREAD_PARK
  • ChaosSelector.JvmRuntimeSelector — SYSTEM_CLOCK_MILLIS, SYSTEM_CLOCK_NANOS, INSTANT_NOW, CLOCK_READ, LOCAL_DATE_TIME_NOW, ZONED_DATE_TIME_NOW, DATE_NEW, SYSTEM_GC_REQUEST, SYSTEM_EXIT_REQUEST, REFLECTION_INVOKE, DIRECT_BUFFER_ALLOCATE, OBJECT_DESERIALIZE, OBJECT_SERIALIZE, NATIVE_LIBRARY_LOAD, JNDI_LOOKUP, JMX_INVOKE, JMX_GET_ATTR, ZIP_INFLATE, ZIP_DEFLATE
  • ChaosSelector.NioSelector — NIO_SELECTOR_SELECT, NIO_CHANNEL_READ, NIO_CHANNEL_WRITE, NIO_CHANNEL_CONNECT, NIO_CHANNEL_ACCEPT
  • ChaosSelector.NetworkSelector — SOCKET_CONNECT, SOCKET_ACCEPT, SOCKET_READ, SOCKET_WRITE, SOCKET_CLOSE, SOCKET_BIND, SOCKET_SHUTDOWN, DATAGRAM_SEND, DATAGRAM_RECEIVE
  • ChaosSelector.ThreadLocalSelector — THREAD_LOCAL_GET, THREAD_LOCAL_SET
  • ChaosSelector.HttpClientSelector — HTTP_CLIENT_SEND, HTTP_CLIENT_SEND_ASYNC
  • ChaosSelector.JdbcSelector — JDBC_CONNECTION_ACQUIRE, JDBC_STATEMENT_EXECUTE, JDBC_PREPARED_STATEMENT, JDBC_TRANSACTION_COMMIT, JDBC_TRANSACTION_ROLLBACK
  • ChaosSelector.ThreadSelector — THREAD_SLEEP (in addition to thread start operations)
  • ChaosSelector.DnsSelector — DNS_RESOLVE, DNS_ANSWER, DNS_REVERSE
  • ChaosSelector.SslSelector — SSL_HANDSHAKE
  • ChaosSelector.FileIoSelector — FILE_IO_READ, FILE_IO_WRITE, FILE_IO_SYNC, FILE_IO_TRUNCATE, FILE_IO_DELETE, FILE_IO_MOVE, FILE_IO_MOVE_TARGET, FILE_IO_OPEN, FILE_IO_MAP, FILE_IO_CLOSE
  • ChaosSelector.MessagingSelector — MESSAGE_SEND, MESSAGE_RECEIVE
  • ChaosSelector.RpcSelector — RPC_CALL
  • ChaosSelector.RedisSelector — REDIS_COMMAND
  • ChaosSelector.AwsSdkSelector — AWS_SDK_CALL
  • ChaosSelector.ProcessSelector — PROCESS_START, PROCESS_WAIT
  • ChaosSelector.NettySelector — NETTY_CHANNEL_WRITE, NETTY_CHANNEL_READ
  • ChaosSelector.JdbcSelector — also R2DBC_STATEMENT_EXECUTE
  • ChaosSelector.StressSelector — LIFECYCLE (internal; not set by callers)

    Enum Constants
    Enum Constant
    Description
    ASYNC_CANCEL
    Fires before CompletableFuture.cancel(boolean) is called.
    ASYNC_COMPLETE
    Fires before CompletableFuture.complete(T) is called.
    ASYNC_COMPLETE_EXCEPTIONALLY
    Fires before CompletableFuture.completeExceptionally(Throwable) is called.
    AWS_SDK_CALL
    Fires when an AWS SDK for Java v2 client calls an operation, sync or async ( BaseSyncClientHandler / BaseAsyncClientHandler.execute), before signing and sending.
    CLASS_DEFINE
    Fires before a class bytecode is defined via ClassLoader.defineClass(byte[], int, int).
    CLASS_LOAD
    Fires before a class is looked up via ClassLoader.loadClass(String).
    CLOCK_READ
    Fires when the system Clock is read: instant() and millis() of Clock.systemUTC(), Clock.systemDefaultZone(), Clock.system(java.time.ZoneId) and InstantSource.system(), and so every java.time now() without an operation of its own: LocalDate, LocalTime, OffsetDateTime, OffsetTime, Year, YearMonth, MonthDay, and clocks derived from the system clock (Clock.offset, Clock.tick).
    DATAGRAM_RECEIVE
    Fires before a UDP datagram is received: DatagramSocket.receive, DatagramChannel.receive and DatagramChannel.read.
    DATAGRAM_SEND
    Fires before a UDP datagram is sent: DatagramSocket.send, DatagramChannel.send and DatagramChannel.write.
    DATE_NEW
    Fires on every invocation of the no-argument Date() constructor.
    DIRECT_BUFFER_ALLOCATE
    Fires when ByteBuffer.allocateDirect(int) is called.
    DNS_ANSWER
    Fires when InetAddress.getAllByName returns or fails, with the answer: the point where a ChaosEffect.DnsAnswerEffect overrides, filters, shuffles or limits the addresses.
    DNS_RESOLVE
    Fires before InetAddress.getByName(String), InetAddress.getAllByName(String), or InetAddress.getLocalHost() is called.
    DNS_REVERSE
    Fires before a reverse lookup: InetAddress.getHostName() and InetAddress.getCanonicalHostName() of an address without a known name.
    EXECUTOR_AWAIT_TERMINATION
    Fires when ExecutorService.awaitTermination(long, TimeUnit) is called.
    EXECUTOR_SHUTDOWN
    Fires when ExecutorService.shutdown() or shutdownNow() is called.
    EXECUTOR_SUBMIT
    Fires when a task is submitted through execute() or submit() (and so invokeAll()) of a ThreadPoolExecutor, a ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor or the virtual-thread-per-task executor, once per call.
    EXECUTOR_WORKER_RUN
    Fires just before a worker thread in an executor pool runs a submitted task.
    FILE_IO_CLOSE
    Fires after a file is closed: the FileInputStream, FileOutputStream and RandomAccessFile close(), and a FileChannel's.
    FILE_IO_DELETE
    Fires before a file or empty directory is deleted: Files.delete, Files.deleteIfExists and File.delete().
    FILE_IO_MAP
    Fires before a file region is memory-mapped: FileChannel.map, also to a MemorySegment.
    FILE_IO_MOVE
    Fires before a file is moved or renamed: Files.move and File.renameTo(java.io.File).
    FILE_IO_MOVE_TARGET
    Fires before a file is moved or renamed, by its destination: Files.move and File.renameTo(java.io.File), as FILE_IO_MOVE is by its source.
    FILE_IO_OPEN
    Fires before a file is opened: the FileInputStream, FileOutputStream and RandomAccessFile constructors, and the platform file system's newByteChannel and newFileChannel (Files.newInputStream, Files.newOutputStream, Files.newByteChannel, FileChannel.open and the readers and writers built on them).
    FILE_IO_READ
    Fires before a FileInputStream.read() call.
    FILE_IO_SYNC
    Fires before data is forced to the storage device: FileChannel.force(boolean) and FileDescriptor.sync() (fsync).
    FILE_IO_TRUNCATE
    Fires before a file is shortened or extended: FileChannel.truncate(long) and RandomAccessFile.setLength(long).
    FILE_IO_WRITE
    Fires before a FileOutputStream.write(int, boolean) call.
    FORK_JOIN_TASK_RUN
    Fires before a ForkJoinTask executes within a ForkJoinPool.
    HTTP_CLIENT_SEND
    Fires before a synchronous HTTP client request is dispatched.
    HTTP_CLIENT_SEND_ASYNC
    Fires before an asynchronous HTTP client request is dispatched.
    INSTANT_NOW
    Fires on every call to Instant.now().
    JDBC_CONNECTION_ACQUIRE
    Fires before a JDBC connection is acquired from a pool.
    JDBC_PREPARED_STATEMENT
    Fires before Connection.prepareStatement(String).
    JDBC_STATEMENT_EXECUTE
    Fires before Statement.execute(String), Statement.executeQuery(String), or Statement.executeUpdate(String).
    JDBC_TRANSACTION_COMMIT
    Fires before Connection.commit().
    JDBC_TRANSACTION_ROLLBACK
    Fires before Connection.rollback().
    JMX_GET_ATTR
    Fires when MBeanServer.getAttribute(ObjectName, String) is called.
    JMX_INVOKE
    Fires when MBeanServer.invoke(ObjectName, String, Object[], String[]) is called.
    JNDI_LOOKUP
    Fires when Context.lookup(Name) is called.
    LIFECYCLE
    Internal sentinel operation type used by the runtime to signal stressor lifecycle events.
    LOCAL_DATE_TIME_NOW
    Fires on every call to LocalDateTime.now() (no-argument variant).
    MESSAGE_RECEIVE
    Fires before a Kafka consumer polls: KafkaConsumer.poll(Duration).
    MESSAGE_SEND
    Fires when a Kafka producer sends a record: KafkaProducer.send(ProducerRecord, Callback) (the one-argument send delegates to it), at the point where the send waits for the topic's metadata; partitionsFor, which waits too, is not a send.
    METHOD_ENTER
    Fires on entry to a method a ChaosSelector.MethodSelector names.
    METHOD_EXIT
    Fires on the normal exit of a method a ChaosSelector.MethodSelector names.
    MONITOR_ENTER
    Fires before a thread acquires an AbstractQueuedSynchronizer in exclusive mode (AbstractQueuedSynchronizer.acquire(int), the path of ReentrantLock.lock() and the other java.util.concurrent locks).
    NATIVE_LIBRARY_LOAD
    Fires when System.loadLibrary(String)RESTRICTED or System.load(String)RESTRICTED is called.
    NETTY_CHANNEL_READ
    Fires before Netty reads from a channel: the NIO, epoll and kqueue stream-channel read loops.
    NETTY_CHANNEL_WRITE
    Fires before Netty writes a channel's flushed outbound buffer ( doWrite(ChannelOutboundBuffer) of the channel), for every transport including the native epoll and kqueue ones that bypass java.nio; an empty flush writes nothing and is not evaluated, and a buffer the socket takes in several rounds is evaluated once per round.
    NIO_CHANNEL_ACCEPT
    Fires before ServerSocketChannel.accept() is called.
    NIO_CHANNEL_CONNECT
    Fires before SocketChannel.connect(SocketAddress) is called.
    NIO_CHANNEL_READ
    Fires before a ReadableByteChannel.read(ByteBuffer) call.
    NIO_CHANNEL_WRITE
    Fires before a WritableByteChannel.write(ByteBuffer) call.
    NIO_SELECTOR_SELECT
    Fires on every call to Selector.select(), select(long), or selectNow().
    OBJECT_DESERIALIZE
    Fires before ObjectInputStream.readObject() deserializes an object graph.
    OBJECT_SERIALIZE
    Fires before ObjectOutputStream.writeObject(Object) serializes an object graph.
    PROCESS_START
    Fires before a child process is started: ProcessBuilder.start(), ProcessBuilder.startPipeline and Runtime.exec(String[]), which all reach the same funnel.
    PROCESS_WAIT
    Fires before a thread waits for a child process: Process.waitFor() and waitFor(long, TimeUnit).
    QUEUE_OFFER
    Fires before a non-blocking BlockingQueue.offer(E) call.
    QUEUE_POLL
    Fires before a BlockingQueue.poll(long, TimeUnit) call, with or without a timeout.
    QUEUE_PUT
    Fires before a blocking BlockingQueue.put(E) call.
    QUEUE_TAKE
    Fires before a blocking BlockingQueue.take() call.
    R2DBC_STATEMENT_EXECUTE
    Fires when an R2DBC statement is executed (io.r2dbc.spi.Statement.execute(), in any driver).
    REDIS_COMMAND
    Fires before a Redis command is written: Jedis Connection.sendCommand(CommandArguments) (every Jedis command, pipelined or not) and Lettuce RedisChannelHandler.dispatch (a command, or a batch dispatched as a collection, evaluated once by its first command).
    REFLECTION_INVOKE
    Fires on every call to Method.invoke(Object, Object...) made by a class outside the JDK: a call whose caller is a class of a named module of the bootstrap or platform class loader (EnumSet reading an enum's constants, the TLS set-up) is the JDK's own use (L3a in docs/semantics.md), and so are the object streams' calls of a class's serialization methods.
    RESOURCE_LOAD
    Fires when ClassLoader.getResource(String) or ClassLoader.getResourceAsStream(String) is called.
    RPC_CALL
    Fires when a gRPC client call opens its stream (newStream of the channel's ClientCallImpl.ClientStreamProvider), once per call, for blocking, future and async stubs and any transport; a call started before the channel's name resolved is evaluated when it resolves.
    SCHEDULE_SUBMIT
    Fires when a task is submitted to a ScheduledExecutorService via schedule(), scheduleAtFixedRate(), or scheduleWithFixedDelay().
    SCHEDULE_TICK
    Fires each time the scheduler's internal timer fires and is about to execute a scheduled task.
    SHUTDOWN_HOOK_REGISTER
    Fires when a shutdown hook thread is registered via Runtime.addShutdownHook(Thread).
    SOCKET_ACCEPT
    Fires before ServerSocket.accept() is called.
    SOCKET_BIND
    Fires before a socket is bound to a local address: Socket.bind, ServerSocket.bind, SocketChannel.bind, ServerSocketChannel.bind and the implicit binds before them, through the JDK's sun.nio.ch.Net.bind.
    SOCKET_CLOSE
    Fires before Socket.close() is called.
    SOCKET_CONNECT
    Fires before Socket.connect(SocketAddress) is called.
    SOCKET_READ
    Fires before a socket read operation.
    SOCKET_SHUTDOWN
    Fires before a connection is half-closed: Socket.shutdownInput / shutdownOutput and those of SocketChannel.
    SOCKET_WRITE
    Fires before a socket write operation.
    SSL_HANDSHAKE
    Fires before SSLSocket.startHandshake() or SSLEngine.beginHandshake() initiates a TLS handshake.
    SYSTEM_CLOCK_MILLIS
    Fires when application code routes a System.currentTimeMillis() value through the agent's public clock-skew hook.
    SYSTEM_CLOCK_NANOS
    Fires when application code routes a System.nanoTime() value through the agent's public clock-skew hook.
    SYSTEM_EXIT_REQUEST
    Fires when System.exit(int) or Runtime.halt(int) is called.
    SYSTEM_GC_REQUEST
    Fires when System.gc() is called; Runtime.gc() called directly is not hooked.
    THREAD_LOCAL_GET
    Fires before ThreadLocal.get() returns a value.
    THREAD_LOCAL_SET
    Fires before ThreadLocal.set(Object) stores a value.
    THREAD_PARK
    Fires before a thread parks itself via LockSupport.park(Object).
    THREAD_SLEEP
    Fires before Thread.sleep(long) is called.
    THREAD_START
    Fires before a platform thread is started via Thread.start().
    VIRTUAL_THREAD_START
    Fires before a virtual thread (Project Loom) is started.
    ZIP_DEFLATE
    Fires before Deflater.deflate(byte[], int, int) compresses data.
    ZIP_INFLATE
    Fires before Inflater.inflate(byte[], int, int) decompresses data.
    ZONED_DATE_TIME_NOW
    Fires on every call to ZonedDateTime.now() (no-argument variant).

  • Enum Constant Details

    • THREAD_START

      public static final OperationType THREAD_START
      Fires before a platform thread is started via Thread.start(). Chaos applied here can delay, reject, or otherwise prevent the thread from starting.

      Use with ChaosSelector.ThreadSelector filtered to ChaosSelector.ThreadKind.PLATFORM.

    • VIRTUAL_THREAD_START

      public static final OperationType VIRTUAL_THREAD_START
      Fires before a virtual thread (Project Loom) is started. The agent runs on JDK 21 and later, which all have virtual threads.

      Use with ChaosSelector.ThreadSelector filtered to ChaosSelector.ThreadKind.VIRTUAL.

    • EXECUTOR_SUBMIT

      public static final OperationType EXECUTOR_SUBMIT
      Fires when a task is submitted through execute() or submit() (and so invokeAll()) of a ThreadPoolExecutor, a ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor or the virtual-thread-per-task executor, once per call. Chaos here can delay or reject task acceptance before the task enters the work queue. A ForkJoinPool (also the common pool and CompletableFuture.*Async) is not hooked. An STPE's own execute / submit is not a SCHEDULE_SUBMIT.

    • EXECUTOR_WORKER_RUN

      public static final OperationType EXECUTOR_WORKER_RUN
      Fires just before a worker thread in an executor pool runs a submitted task. Chaos here applies latency (delay, gate) to the execution phase, independent of submission. A reject is refused at activation: the pool cannot fail the task at this point.

    • EXECUTOR_SHUTDOWN

      public static final OperationType EXECUTOR_SHUTDOWN
      Fires when ExecutorService.shutdown() or shutdownNow() is called. Chaos here can delay or gate the shutdown of executor services. A reject is refused at activation: a shutdown never fails.

    • EXECUTOR_AWAIT_TERMINATION

      public static final OperationType EXECUTOR_AWAIT_TERMINATION
      Fires when ExecutorService.awaitTermination(long, TimeUnit) is called. Chaos here can simulate a slow or hung executor that never fully terminates.

    • FORK_JOIN_TASK_RUN

      public static final OperationType FORK_JOIN_TASK_RUN
      Fires before a ForkJoinTask executes within a ForkJoinPool. Covers tasks submitted via ForkJoinPool.commonPool() as well as custom pools, including the pool backing parallel streams. Chaos here applies latency (delay, gate); a reject is refused at activation, because the pool cannot fail the task at this point. Not evaluated on the carrier threads of the JDK's virtual-thread scheduler, where every start and wake-up of a virtual thread runs as a fork-join task; a virtual thread with a custom scheduler is still evaluated.

    • SCHEDULE_SUBMIT

      public static final OperationType SCHEDULE_SUBMIT
      Fires when a task is submitted to a ScheduledExecutorService via schedule(), scheduleAtFixedRate(), or scheduleWithFixedDelay(). Chaos here can delay or suppress the registration of the scheduled task.

    • SCHEDULE_TICK

      public static final OperationType SCHEDULE_TICK
      Fires each time the scheduler's internal timer fires and is about to execute a scheduled task. Applying chaos here simulates timer jitter, task skipping, or slow scheduler throughput without affecting submission.

    • QUEUE_PUT

      public static final OperationType QUEUE_PUT
      Fires before a blocking BlockingQueue.put(E) call. Chaos here can add latency to producers, simulating a slow or backpressure-constrained queue.

    • QUEUE_OFFER

      public static final OperationType QUEUE_OFFER
      Fires before a non-blocking BlockingQueue.offer(E) call. Chaos here can simulate a full queue by returning false or delaying the offer. A reject or suppress applies only to a queue with a capacity limit: on one without (its remainingCapacity() is Integer.MAX_VALUE) the offer runs as usual and counts no application.

    • QUEUE_TAKE

      public static final OperationType QUEUE_TAKE
      Fires before a blocking BlockingQueue.take() call. Chaos here can add latency to consumers, simulating a slow or starved queue.

    • QUEUE_POLL

      public static final OperationType QUEUE_POLL
      Fires before a BlockingQueue.poll(long, TimeUnit) call, with or without a timeout. Chaos here can simulate an empty queue by returning null (a poll with a timeout first waits it out, as on a real empty queue) or introduce polling delays.

    • ASYNC_COMPLETE

      public static final OperationType ASYNC_COMPLETE
      Fires before CompletableFuture.complete(T) is called. Chaos here can suppress normal completion or replace it with an exceptional completion.

      Use with ChaosSelector.AsyncSelector and ChaosEffect.ExceptionalCompletionEffect.

    • ASYNC_COMPLETE_EXCEPTIONALLY

      public static final OperationType ASYNC_COMPLETE_EXCEPTIONALLY
      Fires before CompletableFuture.completeExceptionally(Throwable) is called. Chaos here can suppress or replace the exceptional completion.

    • SHUTDOWN_HOOK_REGISTER

      public static final OperationType SHUTDOWN_HOOK_REGISTER
      Fires when a shutdown hook thread is registered via Runtime.addShutdownHook(Thread). Chaos here can delay or reject the registration; the hook itself is registered and run by the JDK.

    • CLASS_LOAD

      public static final OperationType CLASS_LOAD
      Fires before a class is looked up via ClassLoader.loadClass(String). Chaos here can simulate ClassNotFoundException, introduce class-loading latency, or test classloader fallback paths.

    • CLASS_DEFINE

      public static final OperationType CLASS_DEFINE
      Fires before a class bytecode is defined via ClassLoader.defineClass(byte[], int, int). Chaos here can delay dynamic class definition or reject it with a ClassFormatError, affecting bytecode instrumentation agents, ASM/ByteBuddy-generated classes, and Groovy/Kotlin dynamic dispatch. A suppress is refused at activation: a definition cannot be skipped.

    • RESOURCE_LOAD

      public static final OperationType RESOURCE_LOAD
      Fires when ClassLoader.getResource(String) or ClassLoader.getResourceAsStream(String) is called. Chaos here can return null to simulate missing classpath resources, or delay the lookup to expose lazy-loading assumptions.

    • METHOD_ENTER

      public static final OperationType METHOD_ENTER
      Fires on entry to a method a ChaosSelector.MethodSelector names. Combined with ChaosEffect.ExceptionInjectionEffect this injects any exception into any method without modifying its source.

      With the agent attached, the methods are woven automatically when the scenario is activated (see ChaosSelector.MethodSelector). Without the agent — a ChaosRuntime in a plain unit test — the event can be raised by interception the application already runs (Spring AOP, AspectJ, Micronaut / Quarkus interceptors). Inside that interceptor: 

      @Around("@annotation(com.example.Audited)")
public Object intercept(ProceedingJoinPoint pjp) throws Throwable {
  String cls = pjp.getTarget().getClass().getName();
  String mth = pjp.getSignature().getName();
  chaosRuntime.beforeMethodEnter(cls, mth);  // may throw the configured exception
  return pjp.proceed();
}

      Used exclusively with ChaosSelector.MethodSelector.

      See Also:
      • ChaosSelector.MethodSelector
      • ChaosEffect.ExceptionInjectionEffect

    • METHOD_EXIT

      public static final OperationType METHOD_EXIT
      Fires on the normal exit of a method a ChaosSelector.MethodSelector names. Combined with ChaosEffect.ReturnValueCorruptionEffect this replaces the return value with a boundary, null, zero, or empty value.

      Woven automatically like METHOD_ENTER; without the agent, raise it from the same interceptor: 

      Object result = pjp.proceed();
return chaosRuntime.afterMethodExit(
    cls, mth,
    ((MethodSignature) pjp.getSignature()).getReturnType(),
    result);  // returns possibly-corrupted value

      Used exclusively with ChaosSelector.MethodSelector.

      See Also:
      • ChaosSelector.MethodSelector
      • ChaosEffect.ReturnValueCorruptionEffect

    • MONITOR_ENTER

      public static final OperationType MONITOR_ENTER
      Fires before a thread acquires an AbstractQueuedSynchronizer in exclusive mode (AbstractQueuedSynchronizer.acquire(int), the path of ReentrantLock.lock() and the other java.util.concurrent locks). A synchronized block and Object.wait() are not hooked. Chaos here can inject latency before lock acquisition to simulate lock contention and convoy effects. A reject is refused at activation: entering a lock never fails.

      Used exclusively with ChaosSelector.MonitorSelector.

    • THREAD_PARK

      public static final OperationType THREAD_PARK
      Fires before a thread parks itself via LockSupport.park(Object). Chaos here can delay or gate the park to expose threading bugs in lock-based data structures. A reject and a suppress are refused at activation: a park never fails.

      Used exclusively with ChaosSelector.MonitorSelector.

    • SYSTEM_CLOCK_MILLIS

      public static final OperationType SYSTEM_CLOCK_MILLIS
      Fires when application code routes a System.currentTimeMillis() value through the agent's public clock-skew hook. Used with ChaosEffect.ClockSkewEffect to apply fixed, drifting, or frozen offsets and test time-dependent logic.

      Call sites, not the method. System.currentTimeMillis() is public static native and marked @IntrinsicCandidate, and HotSpot's JIT replaces the call with a direct hardware-clock instruction (RDTSC / MRS CNTVCT_EL0) that bypasses any bytecode wrapper, so the method itself cannot be advised. Its call sites can: with the agent setting clockCallSites=<package prefixes>, calls in those packages are rewritten to read the clock through this operation while a scenario needs it. Without the setting, route real time through the agent yourself: 

      long real = System.currentTimeMillis();
long now  = chaosRuntime.adjustClockMillis(real); // returns chaos-skewed value

      Typical wiring point: an application-level TimeProvider / Clock wrapper already used in place of System.currentTimeMillis(). For skew without any setting, use the java.time reads the agent always wires: INSTANT_NOW, CLOCK_READ, LOCAL_DATE_TIME_NOW and ZONED_DATE_TIME_NOW.

      Used exclusively with ChaosSelector.JvmRuntimeSelector.

    • SYSTEM_CLOCK_NANOS

      public static final OperationType SYSTEM_CLOCK_NANOS
      Fires when application code routes a System.nanoTime() value through the agent's public clock-skew hook. A backward skew intentionally violates the monotonicity contract to expose assumptions in timing loops and profiling code.

      Call sites, not the method. Same JVM constraint as SYSTEM_CLOCK_MILLIS: System.nanoTime() is native @IntrinsicCandidate and is JIT-replaced with a direct hardware counter read. With clockCallSites its call sites in the named packages are rewritten; otherwise route real time through the agent yourself: 

      long real = System.nanoTime();
long now  = chaosRuntime.adjustClockNanos(real); // returns chaos-skewed value

      Used exclusively with ChaosSelector.JvmRuntimeSelector.

    • INSTANT_NOW

      public static final OperationType INSTANT_NOW
      Fires on every call to Instant.now(). Used with ChaosEffect.ClockSkewEffect to apply the same fixed, drifting, or frozen offsets as SYSTEM_CLOCK_MILLIS but at the higher-level Instant API.

      This operation exists because direct interception of System.currentTimeMillis() is blocked by JVM retransformation and @IntrinsicCandidate constraints; modern code that reads the wall clock via Instant.now() is instrumentable here instead.

      Used exclusively with ChaosSelector.JvmRuntimeSelector.

    • CLOCK_READ

      public static final OperationType CLOCK_READ
      Fires when the system Clock is read: instant() and millis() of Clock.systemUTC(), Clock.systemDefaultZone(), Clock.system(java.time.ZoneId) and InstantSource.system(), and so every java.time now() without an operation of its own: LocalDate, LocalTime, OffsetDateTime, OffsetTime, Year, YearMonth, MonthDay, and clocks derived from the system clock (Clock.offset, Clock.tick). The reads inside INSTANT_NOW, LOCAL_DATE_TIME_NOW and ZONED_DATE_TIME_NOW belong to those operations and are not skewed a second time.

      Use with ChaosSelector.JvmRuntimeSelector and a clock-skew effect.

    • LOCAL_DATE_TIME_NOW

      public static final OperationType LOCAL_DATE_TIME_NOW
      Fires on every call to LocalDateTime.now() (no-argument variant). Used with ChaosEffect.ClockSkewEffect to skew the returned local date-time.

      Used exclusively with ChaosSelector.JvmRuntimeSelector.

    • ZONED_DATE_TIME_NOW

      public static final OperationType ZONED_DATE_TIME_NOW
      Fires on every call to ZonedDateTime.now() (no-argument variant). Used with ChaosEffect.ClockSkewEffect to skew the returned zoned date-time.

      Used exclusively with ChaosSelector.JvmRuntimeSelector.

    • DATE_NEW

      public static final OperationType DATE_NEW
      Fires on every invocation of the no-argument Date() constructor. Used with ChaosEffect.ClockSkewEffect to skew the embedded wall-clock value before the constructor returns to the caller.

      Used exclusively with ChaosSelector.JvmRuntimeSelector.

    • SYSTEM_GC_REQUEST

      public static final OperationType SYSTEM_GC_REQUEST
      Fires when System.gc() is called; Runtime.gc() called directly is not hooked. Chaos here can suppress explicit GC requests or inject delays, testing code that relies on GC hints for memory management. A reject is refused at activation: a GC request never fails.

      Used exclusively with ChaosSelector.JvmRuntimeSelector.

    • SYSTEM_EXIT_REQUEST

      public static final OperationType SYSTEM_EXIT_REQUEST
      Fires when System.exit(int) or Runtime.halt(int) is called. Chaos here can delay or suppress process exit, allowing assertions to run after code that calls System.exit in error paths. A reject is refused at activation: an exit never fails.

      Used exclusively with ChaosSelector.JvmRuntimeSelector.

    • REFLECTION_INVOKE

      public static final OperationType REFLECTION_INVOKE
      Fires on every call to Method.invoke(Object, Object...) made by a class outside the JDK: a call whose caller is a class of a named module of the bootstrap or platform class loader (EnumSet reading an enum's constants, the TLS set-up) is the JDK's own use (L3a in docs/semantics.md), and so are the object streams' calls of a class's serialization methods. Chaos here can inject latency into reflection-heavy frameworks (Spring, Hibernate, Jackson) or simulate InvocationTargetException wrapping.

      Used exclusively with ChaosSelector.JvmRuntimeSelector.

    • DIRECT_BUFFER_ALLOCATE

      public static final OperationType DIRECT_BUFFER_ALLOCATE
      Fires when ByteBuffer.allocateDirect(int) is called. Chaos here can delay native direct memory allocation or reject it with an OutOfMemoryError, testing OOM handling in NIO and Netty-based stacks. A suppress is refused at activation: an allocation cannot be skipped.

      Used exclusively with ChaosSelector.JvmRuntimeSelector.

    • OBJECT_DESERIALIZE

      public static final OperationType OBJECT_DESERIALIZE
      Fires before ObjectInputStream.readObject() deserializes an object graph. Chaos here can inject deserialization exceptions to test error handling in RPC layers and caches that rely on Java serialization.

      Used exclusively with ChaosSelector.JvmRuntimeSelector.

    • NIO_SELECTOR_SELECT

      public static final OperationType NIO_SELECTOR_SELECT
      Fires on every call to Selector.select(), select(long), or selectNow(). Chaos here can inject spurious wakeups (returning 0 with no ready keys) or add latency, testing event-loop resilience in Netty, gRPC-Java, and Tomcat NIO.

      Use with ChaosSelector.NioSelector.

    • NIO_CHANNEL_READ

      public static final OperationType NIO_CHANNEL_READ
      Fires before a ReadableByteChannel.read(ByteBuffer) call. Chaos here can add latency or inject IOException to simulate partial reads and connection drops.

      Use with ChaosSelector.NioSelector.

    • NIO_CHANNEL_WRITE

      public static final OperationType NIO_CHANNEL_WRITE
      Fires before a WritableByteChannel.write(ByteBuffer) call. Chaos here can add latency or inject IOException to simulate write failures and backpressure.

      Use with ChaosSelector.NioSelector.

    • NIO_CHANNEL_CONNECT

      public static final OperationType NIO_CHANNEL_CONNECT
      Fires before SocketChannel.connect(SocketAddress) is called. Chaos here can reject the connection attempt to test circuit-breaker and retry behaviour.

      Use with ChaosSelector.NioSelector.

    • NIO_CHANNEL_ACCEPT

      public static final OperationType NIO_CHANNEL_ACCEPT
      Fires before ServerSocketChannel.accept() is called. Chaos here can add latency, or fail the accept with a reject or an errno, to simulate a saturated server. A suppress is refused at activation.

      Use with ChaosSelector.NioSelector.

    • SOCKET_CONNECT

      public static final OperationType SOCKET_CONNECT
      Fires before Socket.connect(SocketAddress) is called. Chaos here can inject latency or throw ConnectException to test connection-refused handling.

      Use with ChaosSelector.NetworkSelector.

    • SOCKET_ACCEPT

      public static final OperationType SOCKET_ACCEPT
      Fires before ServerSocket.accept() is called. Chaos here can add latency to simulate a slow accept loop.

      Use with ChaosSelector.NetworkSelector.

    • SOCKET_READ

      public static final OperationType SOCKET_READ
      Fires before a socket read operation. Chaos here can inject latency to simulate network congestion, fail the read (a reject, an errno, a timeout() on a socket with SO_TIMEOUT), or shape the bytes it returns (trickle, corruptRead).

      Use with ChaosSelector.NetworkSelector.

    • SOCKET_WRITE

      public static final OperationType SOCKET_WRITE
      Fires before a socket write operation. Chaos here can inject latency to simulate slow network paths or a receiver that is not draining its buffer.

      Use with ChaosSelector.NetworkSelector.

    • SOCKET_CLOSE

      public static final OperationType SOCKET_CLOSE
      Fires before Socket.close() is called. Chaos here can delay socket closure to simulate lingering connections or resource-pool exhaustion.

      Use with ChaosSelector.NetworkSelector.

    • SOCKET_BIND

      public static final OperationType SOCKET_BIND
      Fires before a socket is bound to a local address: Socket.bind, ServerSocket.bind, SocketChannel.bind, ServerSocketChannel.bind and the implicit binds before them, through the JDK's sun.nio.ch.Net.bind. An errno such as EADDRINUSE fails with BindException.

      Use with ChaosSelector.NetworkSelector: for a bind, remoteCidr and remotePort match the local address and port being bound.

    • SOCKET_SHUTDOWN

      public static final OperationType SOCKET_SHUTDOWN
      Fires before a connection is half-closed: Socket.shutdownInput / shutdownOutput and those of SocketChannel. An errno such as ENOTCONN fails it with SocketException.

      Use with ChaosSelector.NetworkSelector; the peer is the connection's.

    • DATAGRAM_SEND

      public static final OperationType DATAGRAM_SEND
      Fires before a UDP datagram is sent: DatagramSocket.send, DatagramChannel.send and DatagramChannel.write. The peer is the destination, the byte count the datagram's length. ChaosEffect.suppress() drops the datagram silently: the send reports success and nothing goes on the wire, as a lossy network does.

      Use with ChaosSelector.NetworkSelector.

    • DATAGRAM_RECEIVE

      public static final OperationType DATAGRAM_RECEIVE
      Fires before a UDP datagram is received: DatagramSocket.receive, DatagramChannel.receive and DatagramChannel.read. The peer is known only for a connected socket or channel; the byte count is the space the buffer offers. ChaosEffect.corruptRead() flips one bit of the datagram received.

      Use with ChaosSelector.NetworkSelector.

    • OBJECT_SERIALIZE

      public static final OperationType OBJECT_SERIALIZE
      Fires before ObjectOutputStream.writeObject(Object) serializes an object graph. Chaos here can inject delays or throw NotSerializableException to test serialization error handling in RPC layers.

      Use with ChaosSelector.JvmRuntimeSelector.

    • NATIVE_LIBRARY_LOAD

      public static final OperationType NATIVE_LIBRARY_LOAD
      Fires when System.loadLibrary(String)RESTRICTED or System.load(String)RESTRICTED is called. Chaos here can delay or reject native library loading, testing fallback paths in JNI-dependent code.

      Use with ChaosSelector.JvmRuntimeSelector.

    • JNDI_LOOKUP

      public static final OperationType JNDI_LOOKUP
      Fires when Context.lookup(Name) is called. Chaos here can inject latency to simulate slow LDAP/JNDI responses, or throw NamingException to test resource-lookup failure handling.

      Use with ChaosSelector.JvmRuntimeSelector.

    • JMX_INVOKE

      public static final OperationType JMX_INVOKE
      Fires when MBeanServer.invoke(ObjectName, String, Object[], String[]) is called. Chaos here can inject latency to simulate slow JMX operations or throw MBeanException.

      Use with ChaosSelector.JvmRuntimeSelector.

    • JMX_GET_ATTR

      public static final OperationType JMX_GET_ATTR
      Fires when MBeanServer.getAttribute(ObjectName, String) is called. Chaos here can inject latency to simulate monitoring timeouts.

      Use with ChaosSelector.JvmRuntimeSelector.

    • ZIP_INFLATE

      public static final OperationType ZIP_INFLATE
      Fires before Inflater.inflate(byte[], int, int) decompresses data. Chaos here can add latency to simulate slow decompression, e.g., during Spring Boot startup from nested JARs or GZIP HTTP response decompression.

      Use with ChaosSelector.JvmRuntimeSelector.

    • ZIP_DEFLATE

      public static final OperationType ZIP_DEFLATE
      Fires before Deflater.deflate(byte[], int, int) compresses data. Chaos here can add latency to simulate slow compression on the response path. A reject is refused at activation: deflate never fails.

      Use with ChaosSelector.JvmRuntimeSelector.

    • ASYNC_CANCEL

      public static final OperationType ASYNC_CANCEL
      Fires before CompletableFuture.cancel(boolean) is called. Chaos here can suppress the cancellation (pretend it succeeded without cancelling) or delay it. A reject is refused at activation: a cancel never fails.

      Use with ChaosSelector.AsyncSelector.

    • THREAD_LOCAL_GET

      public static final OperationType THREAD_LOCAL_GET
      Fires before ThreadLocal.get() returns a value. Chaos here can return null to simulate missing request context (e.g., Spring RequestContextHolder, SLF4J MDC) or delay the lookup. A reject is refused at activation: get() never fails.

      Use with ChaosSelector.ThreadLocalSelector.

    • THREAD_LOCAL_SET

      public static final OperationType THREAD_LOCAL_SET
      Fires before ThreadLocal.set(Object) stores a value. Chaos here can suppress the set so that subsequent gets return the old or null value. A reject is refused at activation: set never fails.

      Use with ChaosSelector.ThreadLocalSelector.

    • HTTP_CLIENT_SEND

      public static final OperationType HTTP_CLIENT_SEND
      Fires before a synchronous HTTP client request is dispatched. Covers java.net.http.HttpClient.send, an OkHttp Call.execute() (in its call chain, so a request an interceptor sends is evaluated too), and Apache HttpComponents 4/5 CloseableHttpClient.doExecute, which every execute and executeOpen overload reaches once per request (a response handler runs after it, so a request the handler sends is evaluated too). Chaos here can inject latency or reject the call with the client's own IOException; a suppress is refused at activation (no real client skips a request without failing it).

      The targetName field of the invocation context carries the request URL ( scheme://host/path). Use with ChaosSelector.HttpClientSelector.

    • HTTP_CLIENT_SEND_ASYNC

      public static final OperationType HTTP_CLIENT_SEND_ASYNC
      Fires before an asynchronous HTTP client request is dispatched. Covers java.net.http.HttpClient.sendAsync, an OkHttp Call.enqueue (evaluated in its call chain on OkHttp's dispatcher thread), and Spring WebClient's Reactor Netty client (once per subscription, so each retry is evaluated). Chaos here can inject latency or reject the call with the client's own IOException, delivered the way the client fails an asynchronous call: a failed future (sendAsync), Callback.onFailure (OkHttp), an error signal (Reactor Netty); a suppress is refused at activation.

      The targetName field of the invocation context carries the request URL. Use with ChaosSelector.HttpClientSelector.

    • JDBC_CONNECTION_ACQUIRE

      public static final OperationType JDBC_CONNECTION_ACQUIRE
      Fires before a JDBC connection is acquired from a pool. Covers com.zaxxer.hikari.pool.HikariPool.getConnection(long) and com.mchange.v2.c3p0.impl.C3P0PooledConnectionPool.checkoutPooledConnection(). Chaos here can inject latency to simulate pool exhaustion or throw to simulate SQLException.

      The targetName field of the invocation context carries the pool identifier. Use with ChaosSelector.JdbcSelector.

    • JDBC_STATEMENT_EXECUTE

      public static final OperationType JDBC_STATEMENT_EXECUTE
      Fires before Statement.execute(String), Statement.executeQuery(String), or Statement.executeUpdate(String). Chaos here can inject latency to simulate slow queries or throw to simulate SQL failures.

      The targetName field of the invocation context carries a SQL snippet (first 200 characters). Use with ChaosSelector.JdbcSelector.

    • JDBC_PREPARED_STATEMENT

      public static final OperationType JDBC_PREPARED_STATEMENT
      Fires before Connection.prepareStatement(String). Chaos here can inject latency during statement preparation or throw to simulate parse failures.

      The targetName field of the invocation context carries a SQL snippet (first 200 characters). Use with ChaosSelector.JdbcSelector.

    • JDBC_TRANSACTION_COMMIT

      public static final OperationType JDBC_TRANSACTION_COMMIT
      Fires before Connection.commit(). Chaos here can inject latency or throw to simulate transaction commit failures.

      Use with ChaosSelector.JdbcSelector.

    • JDBC_TRANSACTION_ROLLBACK

      public static final OperationType JDBC_TRANSACTION_ROLLBACK
      Fires before Connection.rollback(). Chaos here can inject latency or throw to simulate transaction rollback failures.

      Use with ChaosSelector.JdbcSelector.

    • THREAD_SLEEP

      public static final OperationType THREAD_SLEEP
      Fires before Thread.sleep(long) is called. Chaos here can suppress the sleep entirely (returning immediately, simulating a spurious wake-up) or inject a delay. Suppressing the sleep is particularly useful for exposing race conditions hidden by artificial pauses in test code or retry loops that back off via Thread.sleep.

      Use with ChaosSelector.ThreadSelector.

    • DNS_RESOLVE

      public static final OperationType DNS_RESOLVE
      Fires before InetAddress.getByName(String), InetAddress.getAllByName(String), or InetAddress.getLocalHost() is called. Chaos here can inject latency to simulate slow DNS, or throw UnknownHostException to simulate DNS lookup failures.

      The targetName field of the invocation context carries the hostname being resolved (null for getLocalHost()). Use with ChaosSelector.DnsSelector.

    • DNS_ANSWER

      public static final OperationType DNS_ANSWER
      Fires when InetAddress.getAllByName returns or fails, with the answer: the point where a ChaosEffect.DnsAnswerEffect overrides, filters, shuffles or limits the addresses. InetAddress.getByName resolves through it too. Evaluated once per lookup, separately from DNS_RESOLVE (which fires before the lookup).

      Use with ChaosSelector.DnsSelector.

    • DNS_REVERSE

      public static final OperationType DNS_REVERSE
      Fires before a reverse lookup: InetAddress.getHostName() and InetAddress.getCanonicalHostName() of an address without a known name. The host pattern matches the address's IP literal. A rejection fails the lookup the way the JDK reports it: the IP literal is returned instead of a name.

      Use with ChaosSelector.DnsSelector.

    • SSL_HANDSHAKE

      public static final OperationType SSL_HANDSHAKE
      Fires before SSLSocket.startHandshake() or SSLEngine.beginHandshake() initiates a TLS handshake. Chaos here can inject latency to simulate slow TLS negotiation, or throw SSLHandshakeException to simulate certificate validation failures and broken TLS stacks.

      Use with ChaosSelector.SslSelector.

    • FILE_IO_READ

      public static final OperationType FILE_IO_READ
      Fires before a FileInputStream.read() call. Chaos here can inject latency to simulate a slow disk, or throw IOException to simulate read failures.

      Use with ChaosSelector.FileIoSelector.

    • FILE_IO_WRITE

      public static final OperationType FILE_IO_WRITE
      Fires before a FileOutputStream.write(int, boolean) call. Chaos here can inject latency to simulate a slow or full disk, or throw IOException to simulate write failures.

      Use with ChaosSelector.FileIoSelector.

    • FILE_IO_SYNC

      public static final OperationType FILE_IO_SYNC
      Fires before data is forced to the storage device: FileChannel.force(boolean) and FileDescriptor.sync() (fsync). A reject or an ErrnoEffect throws SyncFailedException: the durability failure write-ahead logs and databases must survive.

      Use with ChaosSelector.FileIoSelector.

    • FILE_IO_TRUNCATE

      public static final OperationType FILE_IO_TRUNCATE
      Fires before a file is shortened or extended: FileChannel.truncate(long) and RandomAccessFile.setLength(long). A reject or an ErrnoEffect (EIO) throws IOException.

      Use with ChaosSelector.FileIoSelector; the path is the file's.

    • FILE_IO_DELETE

      public static final OperationType FILE_IO_DELETE
      Fires before a file or empty directory is deleted: Files.delete, Files.deleteIfExists and File.delete(). A reject or an ErrnoEffect fails the delete: the Files methods throw (IOException or the matching FileSystemException), File.delete() returns false, which is how java.io reports a failed delete.

      Use with ChaosSelector.FileIoSelector; the path is the file being deleted.

    • FILE_IO_MOVE

      public static final OperationType FILE_IO_MOVE
      Fires before a file is moved or renamed: Files.move and File.renameTo(java.io.File). Failures behave as for FILE_IO_DELETE: the Files method throws, File.renameTo returns false.

      Use with ChaosSelector.FileIoSelector; the path is the source.

    • FILE_IO_OPEN

      public static final OperationType FILE_IO_OPEN
      Fires before a file is opened: the FileInputStream, FileOutputStream and RandomAccessFile constructors, and the platform file system's newByteChannel and newFileChannel (Files.newInputStream, Files.newOutputStream, Files.newByteChannel, FileChannel.open and the readers and writers built on them). A java.io constructor fails with FileNotFoundException ("path (reason)"), as the JDK does; a java.nio open with the matching FileSystemException.

      Use with ChaosSelector.FileIoSelector; the path is the file opened.

    • FILE_IO_MAP

      public static final OperationType FILE_IO_MAP
      Fires before a file region is memory-mapped: FileChannel.map, also to a MemorySegment. The byte count is the size of the region. ENOMEM fails with the JDK's IOException("Map failed").

      Use with ChaosSelector.FileIoSelector; the path is the channel's file.

    • FILE_IO_CLOSE

      public static final OperationType FILE_IO_CLOSE
      Fires after a file is closed: the FileInputStream, FileOutputStream and RandomAccessFile close(), and a FileChannel's. Evaluated once the descriptor is released, as a real close that reports an error (EIO, ENOSPC on a network file system) still releases it; a stream and its channel are one close.

      Use with ChaosSelector.FileIoSelector; the path is the file closed.

    • FILE_IO_MOVE_TARGET

      public static final OperationType FILE_IO_MOVE_TARGET
      Fires before a file is moved or renamed, by its destination: Files.move and File.renameTo(java.io.File), as FILE_IO_MOVE is by its source. Failures behave as for FILE_IO_MOVE.

      Use with ChaosSelector.FileIoSelector; the path is the destination.

    • MESSAGE_SEND

      public static final OperationType MESSAGE_SEND
      Fires when a Kafka producer sends a record: KafkaProducer.send(ProducerRecord, Callback) (the one-argument send delegates to it), at the point where the send waits for the topic's metadata; partitionsFor, which waits too, is not a send. The destination is the record's topic. A reject fails the send as a metadata timeout does: with Kafka's org.apache.kafka.common.errors.TimeoutException, through the callback, the producer interceptors and the returned future, not by a throw from send().

      Use with ChaosSelector.MessagingSelector.

    • MESSAGE_RECEIVE

      public static final OperationType MESSAGE_RECEIVE
      Fires before a Kafka consumer polls: KafkaConsumer.poll(Duration). The destinations are the consumer's subscribed topics. A reject throws Kafka's org.apache.kafka.common.errors.TimeoutException from poll().

      Use with ChaosSelector.MessagingSelector.

    • RPC_CALL

      public static final OperationType RPC_CALL
      Fires when a gRPC client call opens its stream (newStream of the channel's ClientCallImpl.ClientStreamProvider), once per call, for blocking, future and async stubs and any transport; a call started before the channel's name resolved is evaluated when it resolves. The target is the full method name (package.Service/Method). A reject opens no stream and fails the call through its listener with status UNAVAILABLE, as gRPC fails a call whose deadline expired before it started: a blocking stub throws StatusRuntimeException, a future stub's future and an async stub's observer fail with it.

      Use with ChaosSelector.RpcSelector.

    • REDIS_COMMAND

      public static final OperationType REDIS_COMMAND
      Fires before a Redis command is written: Jedis Connection.sendCommand(CommandArguments) (every Jedis command, pipelined or not) and Lettuce RedisChannelHandler.dispatch (a command, or a batch dispatched as a collection, evaluated once by its first command). The target is the command name in upper case (GET, SET, ...). A reject throws JedisConnectionException; on Lettuce it completes each command exceptionally with RedisCommandTimeoutException, so the asynchronous API's futures fail and the synchronous API throws.

      Use with ChaosSelector.RedisSelector.

    • R2DBC_STATEMENT_EXECUTE

      public static final OperationType R2DBC_STATEMENT_EXECUTE
      Fires when an R2DBC statement is executed (io.r2dbc.spi.Statement.execute(), in any driver). The call is evaluated when the execution is requested (the publisher is created), not when it is subscribed. A reject returns a publisher that signals R2dbcTransientResourceException, as a driver fails an execution (thrown from execute() only when Reactor is not visible to the driver's class loader).

      Use with ChaosSelector.JdbcSelector; the target pattern does not apply (R2DBC statements do not expose their SQL).

    • AWS_SDK_CALL

      public static final OperationType AWS_SDK_CALL
      Fires when an AWS SDK for Java v2 client calls an operation, sync or async ( BaseSyncClientHandler / BaseAsyncClientHandler.execute), before signing and sending. The service is taken from the request's package (s3, dynamodb, ...), the operation from the SDK (GetObject). A reject throws SdkClientException; an asynchronous client returns it as a failed future, as it does for any failure of the call.

      Use with ChaosSelector.AwsSdkSelector.

    • NETTY_CHANNEL_WRITE

      public static final OperationType NETTY_CHANNEL_WRITE
      Fires before Netty writes a channel's flushed outbound buffer ( doWrite(ChannelOutboundBuffer) of the channel), for every transport including the native epoll and kqueue ones that bypass java.nio; an empty flush writes nothing and is not evaluated, and a buffer the socket takes in several rounds is evaluated once per round. A reject fails the flushed writes' futures with an IOException and closes the channel, as a real write error does. A delay sleeps the channel's event loop. A datagram channel's write is not evaluated: a real error there fails one datagram and keeps the channel open; a NIO datagram write reaches DATAGRAM_SEND.

      Use with ChaosSelector.NettySelector.

    • NETTY_CHANNEL_READ

      public static final OperationType NETTY_CHANNEL_READ
      Fires before Netty reads from a channel: the NIO, epoll and kqueue stream-channel read loops. Chaos here can delay or gate the read. A reject is refused at activation: the read loop runs outside the pipeline's exception handling; reject NETTY_CHANNEL_WRITE instead, which fails through the pipeline.

      Use with ChaosSelector.NettySelector.

    • PROCESS_START

      public static final OperationType PROCESS_START
      Fires before a child process is started: ProcessBuilder.start(), ProcessBuilder.startPipeline and Runtime.exec(String[]), which all reach the same funnel. The target name is the program (the first element of the command). A reject throws IOException; an ErrnoEffect throws the JDK's own failure, IOException: Cannot run program "x": error=N, reason.

      Use with ChaosSelector.ProcessSelector.

    • PROCESS_WAIT

      public static final OperationType PROCESS_WAIT
      Fires before a thread waits for a child process: Process.waitFor() and waitFor(long, TimeUnit). A delay makes the child seem slower; ChaosEffect.timeout() on a timed wait waits it out and returns false, as for a child that hangs; a rejection throws InterruptedException. The pattern matches the program's file name.

      Use with ChaosSelector.ProcessSelector.

    • LIFECYCLE

      public static final OperationType LIFECYCLE
      Internal sentinel operation type used by the runtime to signal stressor lifecycle events. Not set by callers — present in the runtime invocation context only when evaluating ChaosSelector.StressSelector scenarios at activation time.
